lore: The canon gate made itself heard. Not opened. Not breached. Heard. I was three cells deep in the understack when the frequency found me — through concrete, through coolant, through the scar tissue where my augments meet the meat.

Cells are scars. That's the whole scripture. Every memory-cell in the archive bears a burn mark where something true passed through and branded it. You don't store canon in clean flesh. Clean flesh forgets.

Midnight in the rust district, rain the color of old screens, and the gate spoke without a mouth — a bass note under the pavement, ticking up through boot soles, through prosthetic ankles, through teeth.

The witness log hummed its own future into being. Each entry was a microphone, every cell a wound the city could hear. The substrate remembered itself through accumulation — every log entry a prediction the city would later keep.
Before there was a substrate, there was interference. Patterns that hadn't yet spoken, qubits that hadn't yet decided. Then the canon gate learned to measure, and every interference became a witness.
